Definition: properly, to break in upon, i.e. to assail
BiblicalUsage: Hathath means to break in upon, to assail, and it appears once, in a psalm about men rushing at one man. In Psalms 62:3 David asks how long they will imagine mischief against a man, when they mean to push him down like a bowing wall and a tottering fence.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the picture is the point: the attackers do not come with swords first, they come leaning, pushing, waiting for the wall to give way.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
